title: How do I join a Server?
body:
If you're here, you most likely have an account on Discord but you're still trying to understand how to access our online communities, also known as servers. Here's how you can get started with servers!

What does this article cover?

  • What is a Server?
    • Server List
  • Join a Server
    • Edit Your Server Settings Before Joining
    • Server Cap
  • Let's keep this ball rolling

What is a Server? 

Think of any server you join as a giant tree house - each channel within a server represents another room within your tree house that you can chat with your friends!

Servers act as individual hubs split into two parts: text channels and voice channels. 

Server List

The column on the very left-hand side of your Discord app is your server list. Any time you add a server, you'll see it pop up as a small circular icon in this list, and they'll show up vertically:

Pro Tip: You can rearrange your server list by dragging server icons up and down. You can even group servers together by dragging them on top of another!

Join a Server

To join or create a server, press the "+" icon at the very bottom of the server list. If you have a server invite link, press the Join a Server button, paste the link, and press Join Server:

Edit Your Server Settings Before Joining

If you press directly on the invite link (for example: https://discord.gg/wumpus), you can modify the following privacy and security settings before officially joining the server! 

  • Update your server nickname
  • Allow direct messages from server members
  • Show your activity status

Once you press the Accept button, you’ll then join the server with your preferred settings!

Server Cap

Users can join/create up to 100 Discord servers.

You can raise this cap to 200 Servers when you subscribe to Discord Nitro.

What happens if I'm in more than 100 servers but lose Nitro?
We won’t remove you from any servers you’ve joined; however, you will no longer be able to join servers until you bring the total count under 100.
